{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA",
    "Given large sample sizes (n=76655 total, with Combined=48846, ICMS Only=11378, Dim Visual Only=9603, Sham=3505, Bright Visual Only=3323), check variance homogeneity using Levene's test",
    "If variance homogeneity violated, use Welch's ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis as robust alternative",
    "Report eta-squared or partial eta-squared for effect sizes"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous variables with significant ANOVA results, perform Tukey HSD post-hoc tests for all pairwise comparisons among the 5 stimulation paradigms",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise z-tests for proportions with correction, or emmeans from logistic model",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs each single-modality condition (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only), Combined vs Sham, and each active condition vs Sham",
    "Report 95% confidence intervals for all pairwise differences"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control for the family of tests across paradigms within each response variable; Bonferroni correction for the number of response variables (5) when summarizing overall findings; given very large sample size, focus on effect sizes and confidence intervals rather than solely p-values",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response and the five performance variables as predictors. This is explicitly recommended because: (1) Stim Paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels, making ordinary linear regression inappropriate; (2) multinomial logistic regression directly models class probabilities; (3) it allows assessment of which performance variables best discriminate paradigms; (4) regularization (elastic net) should be considered given correlated predictors. Alternative: Random Forest or Gradient Boosting for classification if nonlinear relationships suspected, with feature importance to identify key discriminators. The class imbalance (Combined dominates with 63.7% of observations) requires stratified sampling or class weights.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed from experimental design; verify no repeated measures structure within mice across sessions",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals; given n>75000, central limit theorem applies but check for extreme skew (Path Efficiency max=29.8 suggests right skew)",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances across paradigms; Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency show wide ranges suggesting potential heteroscedasticity",
    "Multicollinearity: Check correlations among predictors for multinomial model; Success and Time-to-Target likely negatively correlated",
    "Outliers: Examine extreme values (e.g., Time-to-Target max=201.4, Path Efficiency max=29.8) for data quality",
    "Complete separation check for logistic/multinomial models: Sham has much lower Success (0.27) than others"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham will show significantly worse performance than all active stimulation conditions: lowest Success (0.27 vs 0.67-0.78), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lowest Average Speed (10.7 vs 12.0-12.8), and lowest AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40)",
    "Combined stimulation will outperform or match single-modality conditions, with highest Success (0.78), fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), highest Average Speed (12.8), and highest AD (0.40)",
    "Visual-only paradigms will differ: Bright Visual Only > Dim Visual Only on Success (0.78 vs 0.67) and Time-to-Target (2.61s vs 3.14s)",
    "ICMS Only will perform intermediately, comparable to Dim Visual Only on most metrics",
    "AD (angular dispersion) will be highest for Combined and Bright Visual, lowest for Sham, suggesting more exploratory or directed movement with effective stimulation",
    "Multinomial model will successfully classify paradigms, with Sham most discriminable and Combined vs single-modality conditions most challenging due to class imbalance"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance: Combined represents 63.7% of data (48846/76655), while Bright Visual Only is only 4.3% (3323) and Sham 4.6% (3505), limiting power for comparisons involving rare classes",
    "Cross-sectional summary data only: No access to trial-level data prevents mixed-effects modeling of mouse-specific variation",
    "Unknown temporal structure: Cannot assess learning effects or session-level dependencies",
    "No information on task difficulty, target locations, or trial sequence randomization",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme range (max=29.8) suggesting possible calculation artifacts or outlier trials",
    "Success is binary but treated as mean proportion; no information on number of trials per condition for proper binomial modeling",
    "Single replication (Run ID 296, Replication 3) limits generalizability assessment"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Obtain trial-level data to fit linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts for Mouse and session, enabling proper separation of within-mouse and between-mouse variance; implement the multinomial logistic regression with elastic net regularization to identify minimal sufficient predictors for paradigm classification; conduct equivalence testing (TOST) to formally test whether Combined is non-inferior or equivalent to theoretical optimal performance; and perform sensitivity analyses excluding extreme outliers in Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target to verify robustness of findings."
}
